headline: Mobile element catalogues and genome-typing tools resolve plasmid, species and transmission structure
label: Microbial Mobilome And Genome Typing
summary: proMGE2 expands mobile element cataloguing across habitats while new workflows and an ETEC plasmid study address species typing, SNP clustering and plasmid-host links.
synthesis: The common thread is resolving variable microbial genome content and lineage structure with reusable resources. proMGE2 catalogues more than 16.4 million mobile genetic elements from isolate genomes and MAGs across habitats, with a 5-million-sequence non-redundant set. The ETEC preprint examines plasmid-host associations underlying the distribution of colonization factors, a case where such element-level context matters for virulence plasmid spread. Two workflow preprints address genome-level classification: Robust Cluster Typing assigns genomes to species-level clusters using ribosomal proteins, demonstrated on Campylobacter, and SNP2Cluster-Py provides context-aware core SNP and transmission-cluster analysis, tested on Klebsiella and pneumococcal WGS datasets. Together they pair mobilome-scale resources with lightweight typing and clustering tools, though the items address different layers of the problem rather than a single method.
